concepts.title: Area of a Trapezium
concepts.definition: The area of a trapezium = (1/2) x height x (sum of the parallel sides): Area of a trapezium = h(a + b)/2, where a and b are the parallel sides and h is the perpendicular distance between them.
concepts.key_idea: Half the height times the sum of the parallel sides.

solution_steps.explain: Sum of parallel sides = a + b

concepts.title: Area of a Rhombus
concepts.definition: The area of a rhombus = (1/2) x d1 x d2, the product of the diagonals divided by 2. For example, the diagonals of a rhombus are 7.5 cm and 12 cm; its area is 1/2 x 7.5 x 12 = 45 square cm.
concepts.key_idea: Half the product of the two diagonals.

concepts.title: Area of a Polygon by Splitting
concepts.definition: We split a quadrilateral or polygon into triangles (and trapeziums) and find its area. Area of ABCDE = area of triangle ABC + area of triangle ACD + area of triangle AED. Area of a triangle = 1/2 x base x height; the area of a polygon is the sum of the areas of its parts.
concepts.formula: polygon area = sum of areas of parts; triangle area = base x height / 2
concepts.key_idea: Cut the polygon into triangles and trapeziums and add their areas.

concepts.title: Surface Area of a Cuboid
concepts.definition: The surface area of a solid is the sum of the areas of its faces. The total surface area of a cuboid = 2(lb + bh + hl), where l, b and h are the length, width (breadth) and height of the cuboid respectively. The side walls (the faces excluding the top and bottom) make the lateral surface area of the cuboid: lateral surface area = 2(h x l + b x h) or 2h(l + b).
concepts.formula: total surface area = 2(lb + bh + hl); lateral surface area = 2h(l + b)
concepts.key_idea: Cuboid: TSA 2(lb + bh + hl); walls only LSA 2h(l + b).

concepts.title: Surface Area of a Cube
concepts.definition: All the faces of a cube are square in shape; this makes length, height and width of a cube equal. If each side of the cube is l, the area of each face is l^2. The total surface area of a cube of side l is 6l^2.
concepts.key_idea: Cube has six equal square faces: 6 l squared.

concepts.title: Surface Area of a Cylinder
concepts.definition: The lateral (or curved) surface area of a cylinder is 2 x pi x r x h. The total surface area of a cylinder = pi r^2 + 2 pi r h + pi r^2 = 2 pi r^2 + 2 pi r h = 2 x pi x r x (r + h). Note: we take pi to be 22/7 unless otherwise stated.
concepts.formula: curved surface area = 2 x pi x r x h; total surface area = 2 x pi x r x (r + h)
concepts.key_idea: Cylinder: CSA wraps to a rectangle 2 pi r by h; add two circles for TSA.

concepts.title: Volume of a Cuboid
concepts.definition: Amount of space occupied by a three dimensional object is called its volume. The volume of a cuboid is equal to the product of length, breadth and height: volume of cuboid = l x b x h. Since l x b is the area of its base we can also say volume of cuboid = area of the base x height. Hence height of the cuboid = volume / base area.
concepts.formula: volume = length x breadth x height = base area x height
concepts.key_idea: Cuboid volume is the product of the three dimensions.

concepts.title: Volume of a Cylinder
concepts.definition: Just like the cuboid, volume of cylinder = area of base x height = pi x r^2 x h. A cylinder is formed by rolling a rectangle about its width, so the width becomes the height of the cylinder; or the length of the paper becomes the perimeter of the base, 2 x pi x r.

concepts.key_idea: Cylinder volume is base circle area times height.

concepts.title: Volume and Capacity
concepts.definition: Volume refers to the amount of space occupied by an object. Capacity refers to the quantity that a container holds. Capacity is also measured in terms of litres. The relation between litre and cm^3 is: 1 mL = 1 cm^3, 1 L = 1000 cm^3. Thus, 1 m^3 = 1000000 cm^3 = 1000 L.
concepts.key_idea: Convert volume units: litres are 1000 cubic cm.
